title: hetero-arm-mesh-promoter-with-fidelity-weighting-and-auto-backout
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds heterogenous-arm promotion controller with fidelity-weighted rollback heuristics, new rollout simulator harness, and updated operational runbook. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: We frequently run multi-variant experiments and run mixed hardware pools (A100, H100, CPU-fallback) that require selective promotion and safe backout semantics. Current promote controllers assume a single homogeneous target and provide coarse thresholds. This PR introduces a promotion controller that treats a rollout as a mesh of heterogeneous arms (different model variants, quantization levels, and target hardware classes) and applies fidelity-weighted scoring to decide promotion fractions and automated backout.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Implements HeteroArmMeshPromoter (controller + policy), a lightweight fidelity scorer that aggregates metric deltas with weightings per arm, a non-invasive auto-backout policy tied to an alarm window and quarantine lane, a simulator harness to run replayed traffic experiments locally, and operational docs + playbook entries. Also adds end-to-end tests that run against the simulated workload and small runtime guards to avoid thrashing during concurrent promotes.

Checklist: [x] Design doc attached (ENG-1724) [x] Unit tests for promoter logic [x] E2E simulator scenarios [x] Runbook and rollback playbook updated [x] Backwards-compatible to existing Rollout CRD [ ] Load test in benchmark lab (follow-up PR)

Key design points: - Treat a rollout as a set of arms with independent fidelity priors (quality, latency, cost). - Fidelity-weighted score computes a single promotion score per arm: score = sum(metric_delta * weight) normalized by expected variance. - Promotion fractions are adapted per-arm based on score delta and per-arm capacity budgets. - Auto-backout triggers when fidelity-weighted score crosses alarm threshold for sustained window (configurable). When triggered, traffic is funneled to a quarantine lane and the previous stable snapshot is restored asynchronously. - Simulator supports deterministic replay and stochastic injection to estimate false-positive backouts.

Related: ENG-1725 (simulator improvements), PM-091 (experiment gating requirements), SUP-412 (customer incident that motivated quarantine lane).

Commits summary: - c1e7f3: add HeteroArmMeshPromoter prototype and controller loop - f4a09b: integrate fidelity scorer + config schema - a243d2: simulator harness + deterministic replay engine - b5c9e1: e2e tests and test fixtures - d8f7a0: docs and runbook updates

Files touched (high level): src/controller/promote/hetero_arm_promoter.go, src/controller/promote/policy.go, pkg/simulator/replay_engine.go, tests/e2e/hetero_promote_sim_test.go, configs/rollouts/hetero_policy.yaml, docs/ops/rollout_playbook.md, docs/design/hetero_promoter.md

Testing notes: - Unit tests added for scoring math and tie-breakers. - Simulator scenarios include: clean rollout (no regressions), transient latency spike (should not back out on single short spike), persistent regression on fidelity-weighted metric (should trigger backout). - CI initially failed due to a flaky timing assertion in the simulator; fixed by moving to mock clock.

Operational notes: - Default alarm window is 2m with 3 consecutive evaluation intervals before auto-backout. - Operators can opt-out of auto-backout by policy, and can set a staged quarantine duration. - Runbook added to docs/ops/rollout_playbook.md with play-by-play and recovery commands.

Merge notes: Squash-and-merge after final approval.

For reviewers: focus on the fidelity weighting math (policy.go), the correctness of state transitions (promoter.go) under concurrent promote requests, and the simulator determinism (replay_engine.go).
